A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-based instance-edge framework, renamed from DiffEGG to TRACE. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete to match retained, revised and removed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original instance and panoptic segmentation experiments, backbone comparisons and component analyses in Tables 1-4 and appendix Table G.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation experiments and reports additional component, reconstruction-loss, timestep and edge-detector analyses in Sections 4-6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The core method is retained: PeakKL/EdgeKL/RIP become IEP/ABDiv/BGP, while LoRA, masked Dice plus reconstruction loss, and one-pass inference already appear in v1. As written, Algorithm 1 changes from a descending timestep scan retaining the lower-noise endpoint of the maximum-KL pair to an ascending scan retaining the higher-noise endpoint. v2 also introduces downstream SAM refinement using TRACE-derived seeds in Figure 9.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet training and evaluate UIS on VOC 2012, COCO 2014/2017, LVIS, KITTI, Objects365 and SA-1B, plus tag-supervised panoptic segmentation on VOC and COCO. The additional backbone, SAM and component experiments do not establish new data domains or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds MaskCut+UnSAM and CutLER+CutS3D to Table 1, EPLD to Table 2, and YOLOE+SAM to Figure 9. It also evaluates Canny, HED, PiDiNet and DiffusionEdge as alternative edge sources, and adds Qwen2.5-VL-72B and PixArt-alpha backbone comparisons. Grounding DINO+SAM and Ferret+SAM remain represented in Figure 9 after leaving Table 2.

E3.justification: The main benchmark splits and segmentation metrics remain stable, but v2 substantially expands the evaluation design through component-removal controls, reconstruction-loss removal with SSIM evaluation, timestep strides from 25 to 500, neighborhood variants, additional backbone configurations and SAM refinement. v1's separate adjacent/non-adjacent VOC evaluation and point-annotation control are removed. Newly disclosed optimizer and resolution settings do not establish changed settings for retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds component isolation in Table 3, reconstruction-loss analysis, timestep sensitivity and optimal-timestep distributions in Figure 7, temporal divergence alternatives, and detector-replacement analysis in Figure 10. It also reports neighborhood and merge-threshold robustness findings. Conversely, v1 Table 4's quantitative separation of merging and fragmentation problems and Figure Q's cross-backbone edge examples are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, performance error bars or significance tests. The edge-score mean and standard deviation define method thresholds in both versions; v2's timestep histogram is a supplementary analysis, not performance-uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Most UIS scores, including v1 Table G/v2 Table 8, are unchanged. Table 2 revises DHR+method with Swin-L from 63.9 to 69.8 VOC PQ and 37.5 to 43.1 COCO PQ without explaining the revision. v2 adds substantial ablation and comparator results while removing v1's problem-specific results and COCO 2017 backbone-comparison columns. Reported one-pass latency changes from 190 to 45 ms/image without sufficient timing context for a direct speed comparison. New Figure 2 also reports COCO 2017 scores of 6.2/7.1, conflicting with Table 1's 7.5/7.8.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit forward/reverse SDE formulation and adds a flow-matching velocity objective and reconstruction expression in Appendix D.2. The timestep-selection formulation is revised alongside Algorithm 1. Attention aggregation, spatial KL scoring, masked Dice loss and random-walk mathematics are otherwise substantially retained; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about annotation-free diffusion edges improving UIS and tag-supervised panoptic segmentation remain. v2 adds an explicit 81x inference-speed claim and elevates TRACE-generated SAM seeds and superiority over open-vocabulary detectors into its contributions and conclusion. These extend the efficiency and application claims without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting KL's sensitivity to boundary emergence, reconstruction supervision to reduced noisy-edge overfitting, and conventional detectors' weaker results to texture-sensitive objectives. It also develops SAM complementarity and limitations of depth-based instance separation. v1's explanation attributing low absolute AP to weak initial UIS seeds is removed, while the main merging/fragmentation interpretation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies LoRA rank 64, Adam, weight decay 4e-5 and backbone-dependent input resolutions; Table 6 adds SD3.5-L resource requirements. v1's explicit separate VOC/COCO fine-tuning statement for WPS is omitted. Code-access instructions change from a public repository link to a claimed accompanying Supplementary Material.zip; the archive's contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning against depth-assisted segmentation through CutS3D and CUPS, newer segmentation approaches such as UnSAM, ConceptAttention, EPLD and YOLOE, and conventional or learned edge detectors. Flow matching and newer weakly supervised work are also added. This changes the comparison landscape beyond bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and discussion are extensively rewritten around TRACE terminology and instance-boundary discovery. Background material is redistributed between the method and appendix, ablation and discussion receive separate sections, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added. The title and author block also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and reorganizes the main explanatory figures, combines the method and connectivity illustrations, and moves the propagation and selected feature visualizations into the main text. New component tables, timestep plots, SAM comparisons and detector panels substantially change the presentation. UIS tables are regrouped, references precede the appendices, and appendix navigation is added; most appendix segmentation galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: v2's controlled component, reconstruction and alternative-edge tests strengthen support for the central mechanism, while newer baselines and additional training details improve assessment and reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by removal of v1's targeted merging/fragmentation diagnostic, unexplained Swin-L score and timing revisions, and the new Figure 2/Table 1 numerical inconsistencies. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
